title: Gregorian Calendar
intro: The Gregorian calendar is the civil calendar used in most of the world today. It organises dates according to a solar-year approximation.
structure: A year has twelve unequal months, totaling 365 days in an ordinary year and 366 in a leap year. The month sequence and lengths are listed below; only February changes length.
pattern_note: A year divisible by four is a leap year, except a century year not divisible by 400. Thus 1900 was ordinary and 2000 was a leap year.
example: February 2024 had 29 days and February 2025 had 28; the leap-day rule changes the length of February, not the order of months.
history: Introduced under Pope Gregory XIII in 1582 to correct the Julian calendar's long-term seasonal drift. Adoption was gradual: regional date skips and transition dates differed, and some countries changed centuries later.
model: The resource calculates proleptic Gregorian civil dates. Its UTC-noon day-coordinate domain is JDN 2440588-100000000 through 2440588+99999999, inclusive. Locale-sensitive formatting uses ICU/CLDR. Month and year navigation retain the day number when possible and clamp it to the destination month's length.
limits: Before historical local adoption, the provider extends Gregorian rules backwards mathematically. It does not reconstruct each country's transition from an earlier calendar.
